description:
Human sign-off on the 228 AI-swept questions — the last open Stage 1 gate row (K53-32).

Until now these carried approved_by = 'system' / verified_at null, the state migration 20260804090000 created to mean "an AI sweep set the approved flag; no person has read this". CLAUDE.md constraint 9 does not accept that as verification, so the whole Stage 1 question count rested on machine approval.

What actually happened: John exported the full bank to CSV and sent it to Louwrens, who read it and approved. This records that. It is NOT the tidy-the-column backfill that 20260804090000 forbids — that instruction was against stamping verified_at with no human pass behind it. A human pass happened; leaving the column null would now be the false statement.

HOW THIS BATCH DIFFERS FROM THE 46 (2026-08-03), and how to tell them apart later: the 46 were approved one at a time in the admin UI, so their verified_at values are seconds apart. These 228 share a single identical timestamp, because they were signed off as one CSV rather than item by item. The timestamp is the honest record of that: same approver, same authority, different granularity. Query verified_at = '2026-08-05T09:02:42.538Z' to recover exactly this batch.

Two subsets inside the batch are called out in their per-op why, because they are where a wrong answer is most likely to have survived: the 16 partial citations (source supports the item, not the keyed answer — RR-054 keys "four seconds or more" in heavy rain and no source states any figure) and the 7 deliberately uncited questions (source_basis = uncited_general_knowledge). Both were in the CSV and are covered by the same approval.

Idempotent: reruns compare equal and write nothing.
